h1: Kitlada Hotel — A Quiet Garden Hotel Near Udon Thani Airport That Punches Above Its Star Rating
intro: If you're flying into Udon Thani late at night, or you just want a quiet place away from the bustle of the mall district but easy on the wallet, Kitlada Hotel (Kitlada) is a name that comes up again and again in real reviews · It's a 3-star garden hotel that opened in 2012, set in the Chiang Phin area on Amphur Road, near Udon Thani International Airport and Udon Thani Rajabhat University, about 2.7 km from Central Plaza · Around 40 rooms amid a leafy garden, all with air conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV and free Wi-Fi, plus a restaurant, a massage room and free parking · Guests praise the spacious clean rooms, comfy beds, friendly staff and good value · From about ฿790/night, scoring around 8.4 from real reviews

body.html: Who Kitlada Hotel is right for — To put it as briefly as possible, Kitlada Hotel is a place for people who value quiet and a light price tag more than walking straight to the mall and night market · It isn't a high-rise downtown hotel attached to a shopping center, and it isn't a design-heavy boutique built for photos — it's a 3-star garden hotel of around 40 rooms, planted in the Chiang Phin area on Amphur Road, on the edge of town heading toward the airport and Udon Thani Rajabhat University · It has been open since 2012 and is still running today · Real reviews across several platforms agree that the people it suits are business travellers here for a short trip, families or older guests who drive themselves and want easy parking, people who fly in late and want to sleep near the airport, and parents visiting children studying at Rajabhat · The people who may not find it a good fit are travellers without their own car who want to step out of the hotel and find restaurants or a mall right away, because this spot is fairly quiet and you'll need to call a ride into town · To paint the picture, Kitlada is a "comfortable stay on a budget" hotel that focuses on cleanliness, quiet and value, rather than a hotel you come to for a central location.

Location and getting around — The location of Kitlada Hotel is both a strength and something to understand before you book · The hotel sits at 510 Moo 7, Amphur Road, Chiang Phin, Mueang Udon Thani, a northwestern suburb leaning toward the airport · The clear advantage is that it's close to Udon Thani International Airport (UTH), only about 4–5 km or roughly a 10–15 min drive, which makes it very convenient if you fly in late or have an early flight, with no long ride into the city center · Also nearby is Udon Thani Rajabhat University, about 2.6 km away, while Wat Thippayarat Nimit and Wat Thip Santiwan are within 400 meters, handy for anyone making merit or running errands around here · Meanwhile Central Plaza Udon Thani and UD Town — the shopping and night-market district — are about 2.7 km or roughly a 10 min drive away: too far to walk, but a Grab or a motorbike taxi gets you into town quickly and cheaply · A note that comes up often in reviews is that the hotel sits on a small lane that's fairly hard to find on a first visit, so if you use a navigation app, pin the hotel name precisely and watch the signs carefully — and there aren't many restaurants within walking distance, so guests without their own car should plan ahead for getting around and for meals · For people who drive themselves, this kind of location is actually very comfortable, because traffic is light, access is easy, and there's free parking on site.

"The room was spacious and very clean for the price, the bed was comfy, and the staff were lovely and helpful · I flew in late, drove over and was asleep within minutes, parking was easy, and it was quiet so I slept soundly. Next time I'm in Udon I'll stay here again."

Room types and décor — Kitlada Hotel has around 40 rooms in total, across several tiers to suit your budget and group size · It starts with the Standard Double Room, the lowest-priced standard twin-bed room, good for solo travellers or two people watching their budget · Step up to the Deluxe Double Room, which is roomier and has a minibar · the VIP King Room is the popular king-bed option, a notch more spacious again · and the largest is the Suite, with a private entrance and more living space, good for those who want more privacy or are staying several nights · Every room has air conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, blackout curtains and a private bathroom with a shower, and some have a sofa and a bathtub · The décor is warm and easy on the eye, the kind you find in a well-kept upcountry hotel — not flashy, but clean and genuinely functional · Many reviews agree that the rooms are larger than expected at this price, very clean, and the beds are comfy, a point guests come back to again and again · The quiet is a plus too, because the location is set back from the main road and within a garden, making for easy sleep · A note found in reviews is that some rooms still don't have a smart TV, and some amenities are basic — for instance, the towels provided are limited in number and asking for extra may carry a small charge · If a particularly spacious room or a bathtub matters to you, go for the VIP King or Suite and request it when you book.

Facilities and common areas — Let's be straight up front: Kitlada is a small 3-star hotel, so it doesn't have the lavish common areas of a big hotel, and there is no swimming pool · This matters for anyone planning to swim or bring kids to splash around, so it's worth knowing before you book · But what it does have fits a relaxed stay well · The highlight here is the leafy garden and the quiet that many reviews mention as a break from the busyness of the city, with outdoor seating and a terrace for a morning coffee · There's a massage room for easing tired muscles after a day of travel or errands · There's an on-site restaurant and bar, room service, a taxi-booking service, laundry service (for a fee) and a 24-hour front desk · Importantly for those who drive themselves, there's free on-site parking that's wide and easy, with no fighting for a space like at a downtown hotel · Wi-Fi is free both in the rooms and in the common areas · Overall, Kitlada's facilities lean toward the simple and genuinely usable in the manner of a small hotel, rather than the full kit of a big one, which fits the price and the concept here.

Food and the restaurant — Breakfast is a point talked about both positively and with caveats · Breakfast is usually included in the room rate, and many reviews say it's tasty, with a decent choice of Thai and Isan dishes served fresh in a pleasant garden setting · The kitchen and serving team earn praise for being friendly · But to be fair, some voices in reviews, especially from foreign travellers, feel the breakfast is fairly basic for those used to Western menus — bacon or high-quality coffee, for instance, may be in short supply — and when everyone comes down at once the restaurant can get a bit busy and noisy · For other meals, because the location is fairly quiet and there aren't many restaurants within walking distance, many people choose to drive or call a Grab into town to eat at Central Plaza, UD Town or one of Udon's well-known Isan restaurants, about a 10 min trip · Those who drive themselves have it much easier here, since they can roam freely for food around town · In short, the food at Kitlada is enough for breakfast and a relaxed stay, but it isn't a hotel you come to in order to eat every meal in — plan lunch and dinner outside.

Service — Service is the strength most consistently praised at Kitlada Hotel · The reception and the team are mentioned very often as friendly, smiling, helpful and attentive, especially with helping to call rides, recommending restaurants and sights, giving directions to guests who can't find the hotel, and a hassle-free check-in and check-out · Being a small hotel makes the care feel personal and closer than at a big one · Many say it's a big reason they return or recommend it · That said, to be even-handed, some voices in reviews from foreign travellers say a few staff have limited English, so working out certain details can take a little time or some gestures · For Thai guests this is hardly an issue, and on the whole the team's friendliness more than makes up for the language gap · Service, then, is one of the hearts of why this place scores well overall.

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — Pulling together Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, Expedia and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: spacious, clean rooms that beat the price are talked about most, comfy beds, a quiet atmosphere for sound sleep, friendly and helpful staff, decent breakfast, free parking that's convenient for self-drivers, proximity to the airport for those flying in late, and value that many sum up as "more than you pay for" · TripAdvisor places it around #16 of 73 hotels in Udon Thani, which is good for a budget hotel · On the caveat side: the most-mentioned point is the fairly quiet, hard-to-find location, set on a small lane, far from the mall and market district, requiring a ride into town, with few restaurants within walking distance · Next come no swimming pool, some rooms without a smart TV, breakfast that's fairly basic for those used to Western menus, limited towels with a small charge for extras, and a few staff with limited English · These gripes are mostly things you can manage by setting expectations correctly and having your own car or a travel plan, rather than big problems that keep people from coming back.

"Great value at this price, the room was clean and quiet, ideal for self-drivers · The only downside is the hotel is a bit hard to find on the first visit because it's down a lane, and there aren't many restaurants within walking distance, so you have to drive into town — but it's only ten minutes to the mall."

Price and value — The starting price for a Standard room is around ฿790/night in normal periods, rising to about ฿1,100–1,200 when it's busy or there's an event in town · Deluxe and VIP King rooms run about ฿900–1,300, and the Suite about ฿1,400 and up depending on the season · Most rates already include breakfast and free parking · Compared with downtown Udon hotels like Centara Udon or Civilize Hotel, which cost more and sell their mall-side location, Kitlada's clear advantage is a lighter price and a spacious, clean room in a quiet setting, plus proximity to the airport and free parking that's easier than at a downtown hotel · For people with their own car who weigh quiet and a tight budget, or who need to sleep near the airport, the value at Kitlada is well and truly worth it · For those without a car who want to walk to the mall or night market directly, the daily fare into town may eat into the cheaper room rate, so weigh it up carefully before choosing · In the cool season (December–February), the high season for Isan, prices and availability tighten — book ahead and compare across several platforms.

Good to know before you book — A few things help make a stay at Kitlada smoother · One, if you drive yourself or use Grab, pin the hotel name precisely in your navigation app, because the hotel is down a small lane that's hard to find on a first visit — watch for the signs and call the front desk for directions · Two, if you don't have your own car, budget time and money for rides into town for meals and shopping, because there are few places within walking distance · Three, this hotel has no swimming pool, so if you mean to swim, consider somewhere else · Four, if you want a particularly spacious room or a bathtub, choose the VIP King or Suite and request it when booking · Five, on the limited towels, if you need more than usual, tell the front desk in advance (there may be a small charge) · Six, for those flying in late, the location near the airport is an advantage — you can notify your arrival time in advance since the front desk is open 24 hours · Seven, in high season and during events in town rooms fill fast, so book ahead and pick a Free Cancellation rate in case your plans change.

The verdict — From all the real reviews, Kitlada Hotel is best for people who weigh quiet, value and the convenience of driving themselves — flying in late and wanting to sleep near the airport, here for a short trip, visiting children studying at Rajabhat, or just wanting a clean, quiet stay on a budget · Spacious clean rooms that beat the price, comfy beds, a quiet garden setting, friendly staff, breakfast included and free parking make it a value pick among Udon's budget hotels · The trade-off to accept is a fairly quiet, hard-to-find location, far from the mall and market district, requiring a ride into town, no swimming pool, and the basic facilities of a small hotel · If you don't have a car and want to walk straight to Central or UD Town, a downtown hotel like Centara Udon may suit you better · But if you have a car, are after quiet, and want a good room at a light price, Kitlada Hotel does exactly that well — and it's why guests score it highly and come back.
